extracted.intended_audience: H-1B petitioners, employers, immigration attorneys, stakeholders, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for DHS's rule implementing a wage-weighted H-1B cap selection process, explaining goals (prioritize higher-skilled/high-paid beneficiaries), responses to public comments, and operational considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize relatively higher-skilled, higher-valued, or higher-paid foreign workers
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS: the weighted selection process will "favor relatively higher-skilled, higher-valued, or higher-paid foreign workers, consistent with the congressional intent of helping U.S. employers hire highly skilled aliens to address gaps in the U.S. workforce."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule implements a wage-weighted selection to increase selection probability for beneficiaries with wages corresponding to higher wage levels (e.g., level III and level IV). DHS frames this as returning the program to its original purpose of attracting highly skilled temporary workers and enhancing U.S. competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect the wages, working conditions, and job opportunities of U.S. workers
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS repeatedly states the rule will "better protect the wages, working conditions, and job opportunities of U.S. workers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expected outcomes include reducing hiring of lower-paid, lower-skilled foreign workers who depress wages and displace U.S. workers (particularly in IT/STEM fields), expanding employment prospects for U.S. citizens and recent graduates, and benefiting lawful permanent residents and other legal immigrant workers similarly affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve program integrity and reduce gaming/fraudulent registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters argued and DHS agreed the new selection process would "improve both the integrity of the registration program and the H-1B program overall."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS asserts the wage-based weighting will discourage "fake registrations" and manipulative practices by employers and staffing firms, thereby restoring trust in the program. The rule is presented as a tool to reduce systematic exploitation of the H-1B lottery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain opportunity for employers and beneficiaries at all wage levels
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS: the rule should favor higher-paid workers "while maintaining the opportunity for employers to secure H-1B workers at all wage levels."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The weighted lottery is intended to increase chances for higher-wage beneficiaries but not to preclude selection of registrations tied to lower corresponding wage levels; employers seeking lower-wage workers may still participate and have a chance at selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use salary/wage level as a reasonable proxy for skill level
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS: "salary generally is a reasonable proxy for skill level."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS cites prior wage methodology analyses and economic literature to justify using prevailing wage levels as a practical metric to weight selection toward workers expected to have higher skills or value. This is presented as a core normative and methodological justification for the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain an element of randomness while increasing weighted chances
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS intends to "retain the elements of uncertainty and randomness" but increase chances for higher-wage beneficiaries (e.g., level IV >61%, level III >45%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS argues it is important to keep some randomness to preserve opportunity while using weights to meaningfully change selection probabilities in favor of higher-paid, higher-skilled beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase predictability and reduce uncertainty for highly-paid beneficiaries
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS claims the rule will "increase the chances that a registration for a highly skilled, highly paid alien will be selected" and thereby increase certainty and predictability relative to the previous uniform-random lottery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS contrasts current ~30% chance under random lottery with substantially higher modeled probabilities under weighting; the rule is thus evaluated by its capacity to make selection outcomes more predictable for higher-wage candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid creating a "pay-to-play" system and address fairness/equal opportunity concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters warned the weighted selection would be unfair, favoring large corporations and the wealthy and amount to "pay-to-play." DHS responds it does not view the system as pay-to-play and frames wages as a proxy for skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule is evaluated on whether it reasonably balances fairness concerns—ensuring it does not unjustly exclude skilled workers from diverse backgrounds—while advancing the program's congressionally intended purpose. DHS emphasizes that the approach still allows participation across wage levels to mitigate fairness risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve transparency and understandability of the selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: Some commenters argued weighting would "complicate" the selection process and undermine trust due to complexity; DHS asserts parameters were made clear and the process will be transparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A criterion for acceptability is that the weighted method be sufficiently transparent and explained to the public so participants understand how weights affect odds. DHS asserts sufficient public notice and operational readiness to address transparency concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not restrict statutory visa cap or preclude companies from selection
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS: "this rule does not restrict the number of H-1B visas available under the statutory cap, nor does it preclude any company from selection in the H-1B cap selection process."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An important legal/operational constraint is that weighting must operate within the statutory annual cap and preserve access for petitioners; the rule must be designed and implemented consistent with the cap and existing statutory constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support startups, small businesses, and critical-sector employers' access to talent
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters expressed concern weighting would disadvantage startups and small businesses that cannot match large-company salaries; DHS responds the rule "will benefit companies of all types, including startups" and does not treat them differently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should consider whether the rule permits startups and smaller firms to attract talent (e.g., by allowing employers to offer wages above prevailing when they value a candidate) and whether the tradeoffs in cost versus selection odds are reasonable for small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote entry-level opportunities and benefit recent graduates and international students with high offers
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS agrees the rule will "help to better protect the wages, working conditions, and job opportunities of U.S. workers, including U.S. college students and recent graduates," and will benefit international students with high-wage offers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metrics include projected decreases in level I petitions (cited DHS data: a decrease of 10,099 annually) and an assessment of whether entry-level U.S. hires and recent graduates gain improved employment prospects as intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid incentivizing offshoring/outsourcing as an unintended consequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters worried the rule would push employers to offshore work or hire cheaper offshore resources; DHS disagrees and states the rule is not expected to cause outsourcing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A valid evaluation criterion is whether the rule leads to measurable increases in offshoring or reductions in domestic hiring; DHS references literature and argues the rule neither changes the statutory cap nor forces firms to offshore as an inevitable response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational and technical feasibility of implementing the weighted selection
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS/USCIS: "USCIS is fully prepared to implement the weighted selection process from an operational and technical perspective in time for the upcoming H-1B cap season."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptability of the rule depends on demonstrable operational readiness (systems, timing, clarity of parameters) so that the weighted lottery can be executed reliably and on schedule; DHS claims adequate notice and preparation.
